text:
ajay: ran a perf sweep against the hybrid FP8/INT4 rollout and hit a pretty nasty regression on p3-16x. avg tail latency up ~35% for long-context chat (seq=2048). attaching short trace and flame output below. anyone seen this pattern before?

maria: ugh. can you paste the nsys snippet? small traces are easiest to eyeball.

ajay: pasted below. note the kernel switch: triton_gemm_fp8_sm80 -> cutlass_hybrid_int4_fp8_sm86 in the middle of the stream; timing shows the CUTLASS kernel much heavier per-token.

```
# nsys summary (trimmed)
Time(ns) | Kernel                              | Calls | Avg(ms)
-----------------------------------------------
1.2e9    | triton_gemm_fp8_sm80                | 432   | 0.42
3.5e8    | cutlass_hybrid_int4_fp8_sm86        | 128   | 1.15
4.1e8    | kv_cache_lookup                      | 56000 | 0.003
```

ajay: also noticed batching heuristics changed: continuous-batcher size jumped from 8->16 after the kernel switch, causing more KV cache churn (more KV misses).

ken: interesting. that kernel name suggests arch-detection picked sm86 path, but node is sm80. could be we fall back to a different codegen because of feature detection mismatch. did the build flags for CUTLASS change in the last release?

lucy: yep — CI merged the new cutlass build with `-arch=sm_86 -DUSE_WARP_INTRINSICS` for better throughput on newer machines. but we included a runtime arch-prober that should pick the right kernel. maybe the prober is misreporting on that instance.

maria: ajay, can you dump the prober logs? look for `arch_query` + `kernel_selector` lines. if prober flips mid-stream that explains kernel mix.

ajay: prober excerpt: `arch_query: sm80`, then later `kernel_selector: prefer_cutlass_sm86 for model=redwood-65b quant=hybrid`. suspect the selector has a bug: it prefers cutlass_sm86 if a single node in pool reports sm86 capability elsewhere (cross-node inference routing).

devin: that matches a recent change: routing policy can route by capability with soft-fallthrough. if a request hops to a node with sm86-capable pool, selector favors cutlass path even for sm80 workers because we allowed kernel compatibility across nodes. that's dangerous.

lucy: actionable: enforce node-local kernel compatibility in selector, or revert the compatibility heuristic. quick mitigation: set env `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=triton_fp8` on the p3-16x pool to pin triton path. we should schedule a rollback for the cutlass build change if the selector fix isn't trivial.

ken: also worth checking KV cache alignment — bigger batches increased prefix sharing assumptions. if batches combine heterogeneous prefixes we lose cache hits. bumping batch size mandates a caching policy change.

ajay: repro steps I used:
```
# repro script (simplified)
export REDWOOD_PROBER_VERBOSE=1
export REDWOOD_BATCH_MAX=16
run_loadtest --model redwood-65b-hybrid --seq 2048 --duration 10m --concurrency 48
nsys profile --output=trace.nsys ./run_loadtest ...
```

maria: thanks. plan: 1) pin kernel on affected pool (short-term), 2) revert cutlass build flags in canary (if perf regression reproduces), 3) patch selector to prefer node-local kernels + add a prober sanity check, 4) add a batching->kv policy gate so we don't increase batch size beyond kv hit threshold. I'll own (1) and (3). ken, can you look at (4)? lucy/ajay, can you validate the revert (#2) with one canary?

ken: on it. I'll add a perf guard in batching config that enforces `if estimated_kv_miss_rate > 0.12 then max_batch=8` and wire it to real-time KV metrics.

lucy: i'll revert the cutlass flags in a canary branch and run the same loadtest. timeline: 2 hours for build + 1 hour canary run.

ajay: pinned pool now via: `rb set-pool-env p3-16x REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=triton_fp8` — immediate latency back to baseline in small smoke test :thumbsup:. running the full load now, will update.

runtime-bot: deploy p3-16x env var set by ajay at 2026-03-18T14:23:45Z (meta).

ajay: full load shows 4% regression remains, but that looks like noise. major spike gone. uploading trimmed traces to https://perf.gist/redwood/1823456789 for postmortem.

maria: great. next steps: file a bug for selector compatibility heuristics, add unit test for prober flip case, and schedule build revert if canary confirms. i'll open a brief RFC for the kv->batch gating.

ken: logging backlog: `kv_miss_rate`,`batch_size`,`kernel_choice` for 48h to validate baseline before we re-enable change. I'll add those metrics to the console dashboard.

lucy: can everyone ack if they picked up the assigned items?

ajay: ack (traces + follow-up).

maria: ack (selector patch + bug).

ken: ack (kv gate/metrics).

devin: will help if revert is needed.

lucy: ack (canary revert build).

ajay: thanks all, I think this explains the regression: cross-node kernel preference + larger batch = cutlass path on non-sm86 nodes + higher per-token cost + KV churn. we'll keep kernel pin until selector is hardened.
